docs.title: Taxonomy variables
docs.text:
taxonomy_id is the name of the taxonomy in the format: , where:

  • CCN stands for "Common Cell type Nomenclature"
  • YYYYMMDD represents an 8 digit date format (Y=year, M=month, D=day)
  • T is a 1-digit taxonomy counter, which allows up to 10 taxonomies on the same date

If more than 10 taxonomies are being generated on a single date, it is reasonable to increment or decrement the data by a day to ensure uniqueness of taxonomies. More generally, to keep taxonomy IDs unique, please select a taxonomy_id NOT IN THIS TABLE, and add your taxonomy_ID to the table as needed. Strategies for better tracking of taxonomy IDs are currently under consideration , including a Cell Type Taxonomony Service currently in development for Allen Institute taxonomies, additional databasing options for the Brain Initiative - Cell Census Network (BICCN), a Cell Annotation Platform (CAP) under development as part of the Human Cell Atlas, and likely other options. One future goal will be to centralize these tracking services and replace the above table.

taxonomy_author is the name of a point person for this taxonomy (e.g., someone who is responsible for it's content). This could either be the person who built the taxonomy, the person who uploaded the data, or the first or corresponding author on a relevant manuscript. By default this person is the same for all cell_sets; however, there is opportunity to manually add additional aliases (and associated assignees and citations that may be different from the taxonomy_author) below.

taxonomy_citation is a the citation or permanent data identifier corresponding to the taxonomy (or "" if there is no associated citation). Ideally the DOI for the publication will be used, or alternatively some other permanent link.

anatomicstructure. This represents the location in the brain (or body) from where the data in the taxonomy was collected. Ideally this will be linked to a standard ontology via theontology_tag`. In this case, we choose "middle temporal gyrus" from "UBERON" since UBERON is specifically designed to be a species-agnostic ontology and we are interested in building cross-species brain references. It is worth noting that these structures can be defined separately for each cell set at a later step, but in the initial set-up only a single structure can be input for the entire taxonomy.

docs.title: Cell set variables
docs.text:
• cell_set_accession^: The unique identifier (cell set accession id) assigned for each cell set of the format _<#>, where CS stands for cell set, matches the taxonomy_id (see above), and the # is a unique number starting from 1 for each cell set.
  • original_label: The original cell type label in the dendrogram. This is used for QC only but is not part of the CCN.
  • cell_set_label: A label of the format <#>. If only a single first_label was input above, these numbers will match the <#> from cell_set_accession. This used to be part of the CCN and is now deprecated, but critical but useful for coding purposes.
  • cell_set_preferred_alias^: This is the label that will be shown in the dendrogram and should represent what you would want the cell set to be called in a manuscript or product. If the CCN is applied to a published work, this tag would precisely match what is included in the paper.
  • cell_set_aligned_alias^: This is a special tag designed to match cell types across different taxonomies. We discuss this tag in great detail in our manuscript, and will be discussed briefly below. As output from build_nomenclature_table, this will be blank for all cell sets.
  • cell_set_additional_aliases^: Any additional aliases desired for a given cell set, separated by a "|". For example, this allows inclusion of multiple historical names. As output from build_nomenclature_table, this will be blank for all cell sets.
  • cell_set_structure^: The structure, as described above. Can be modified for specific cell sets below. Multiple cell_set_structures can be given separated by a "|".
  • cell_set_ontology_tag^: The ontology_tag, as described above. Can be modified for specific cell sets below. Multiple cell_set_ontology_tags can be given separated by a "|", and must match cell_set_structure above.
  • cell_set_alias_assignee: By default the taxonomy_author, as described above. In this case, if aliases are assigned by different people, additional assignees can be added by separating using a "|". The format is [preferred_alias_assignee]|[aligned_alias_assignee]|[additional_alias_assignee(s)]. If aliases are added without adding additional assignees it is assumed that the assignee is the same for all aliases.
  • cell_set_alias_citation: By default the taxonomy_citation, as described above (or can be left blank). In this case, if preferred (or other) aliases are assigned based on a different citation, additional citations can be added by separating using a "|", with the same rules as described by cell_set_alias_assignee. Ideally the DOI for the publication will be used (or another permanent link).
  • taxonomy_id^: The taxonomy_id, as described above. This should not be changed.

docs.title: Template files and scripts
docs.text:
The main script that drives the template files are located at: src/scripts/template_generation_tools.py

Functions to drive templates: - generate_ind_template -> src/templates/CCN20230722.tsv

Generates the named individuals ROBOT template.

  • generate_base_class_template -> src/patterns/data/default/CCN20230722_class_base.tsv

Main DOSDP template file that drives the class generation. This file is merged with the _class_curation.tsv at runtime and the final class template is generated. Merged template uses the src/patterns/dosdp-patterns/taxonomy_class.yaml template.

  • generate_curated_class_template -> src/patterns/data/default/CCN20230722_class_curation.tsv

This template enables us to do the manual curations without touching the programmatically generated base class template. This file is not actively used in the current workflow.

  • generate_marker_gene_set_template -> src/patterns/data/default/CCN20230722_marker_set.tsv

Marker set template. Uses the src/patterns/dosdp-patterns/taxonomy_marker_set.yaml template.

  • generate_nsforest_marker_gene_set_template -> src/patterns/data/default/CCN20230722_nsforest_marker_set.tsv

NSforest marker set template. Uses the src/patterns/dosdp-patterns/taxonomy_marker_set.yaml template.

There are some legacy template functions in the code (such as homology, taxonomy etc.) that are not actively used in the current workflow.

docs.title: Regenerate templates
docs.text:
Delete the existing template you want to regenerate and run the following command:

cd src/dendrograms
make

docs.text:
• In the server navigate to the OLS folder: 

    cd  /home/ubuntu/OLS/ols4

  • Set some env variables: 

    export OLS4_CONFIG=./dataload/configs/sanger.json

  • Shutdown the OLS server 

    JAVA_OPTS="-Xms5G -Xmx25G" docker compose down -v

  • Restart the OLS server (This operation will take approx 10 minutes)

docs.text:
Status: Draft

Last updates: 2nd January 2021

docs.title: Taxonomy in OWL
docs.text:
iri schema:

IRIs are derived from Allen Dendrogram node names

Current (temporary) solution:

CS201810310_140 -> http://www.semanticweb.org/brain_data_standards/AllenDend_CS201810310_140

Warning - this scheme will change once the Allen releases it's own IRI scheme.

Logic:

Dendrograms nodes are represented as OWL individuals, classified as cell clusters, and stand in subcluster_of relationships (OPA) to each other.

Annotations:

rdfs:label =

skos:preflabel =

OboInOwl:ExactSynonym =

e.g.

The subcluster_of objectProperty is currently a custom object property for this project. This should be generalised.

docs.title: Data Driven Classes
docs.text:
iri schema:

We are currently using (unstable!) UUIDs. This is a temporary expedient. Proposed change: switch to dendrogram node ID derived scheme. Once the ontology is sufficiently mature, these will be deprecated and replaced by CL IDs/IRIs with standard mapping.

logic:

Each class is EquivalentTo: cell and (has_exemplar value {dendogram node Individual})

When combined with the property chain axiom: subcluster_of o has_exemplar -> has_exemplar

Reasoning => classification following the dendogram

docs.title: Property driven classification
docs.text:
All terms get a taxon restriction (in_taxon some {NCBI_taxon}) and a has_soma_location relationship to the relevant brain region.

Additional subclassing axioms name CL parent classes or use simple anonymous class expressions to name classes.

docs.title: Markers
docs.text:
Genes are modelled as classes

Marker genes are related to Individuals via expresses, eg.

TBD: Add axioms to bridge these markers from Individuals to Classes, or change build/schema to attach them directly to classes?

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The next WMBO release will promote about 457 WMBv1 cell sets to CL. docs/wmbv2_cl_promotion.md describes how they are chosen. Their names go into CL, so they must be accurate.

Today a promoted term's label comes from the DOSDP template "%s %s (%s)": taxonomy label + Gross_cell_type (the nearest CL term on the node or an ancestor) + taxon. This goes wrong in three ways: - Redundancy. Taxonomy tokens repeat what the CL head term says: - STR D1 Gaba direct pathway medium spiny neuron (Mmus) - CBX MLI Megf11 Gaba molecular layer interneuron (Mmus) - VLMC NN vascular leptomeningeal cell (Mmus) - Astro-TE NN_3 astrocyte (Mmus) - Misleading neurotransmitters. The neurotransmitter (NT) in the label is fixed at subclass level, or comes from the CL term, but not all clusters underneath carry it. - CB PLI Gly-Gaba has GABA-only clusters. - Every cluster of MB-MY Tph2 Glut-Sero is annotated either Sero or Glut, never both. - The curated name for 21 MB Dopa (merged into SUBC_215) is "midbrain GABAergic neuron". - Locations fixed at subclass level. Supertypes and clusters often have no cells in some of the regions their label names.

Goal: give every CL-promoted term a curated final name that is accurate and not redundant. Existing taxonomy labels stay as exact synonyms and are not changed.

Sequencing: promotion review and action → CL parent mapping → naming → release. The CL parent supplies the head noun of the name, so naming comes after mapping.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. The override replaces the whole name. The final label comes verbatim from defined_class_name in the WMBO_CCN20230722_class_curation sheet, with no template parts appended. Every CL-promoted term gets one; no template-generated label ships in CL. The PCL terms are out of scope for now.
  2. Taxonomy labels are left alone. They are already exact synonyms (Synonyms_from_taxonomy), and the v2 label is added as an exact synonym (with a CCN20251031 xref).
  3. Neurotransmitters in the name:
  4. Drop any NT mention that isn't supported by all v1 clusters under the term, using neurotransmitter_accession.
  5. This applies to taxonomy tokens (Glut, Gaba, Gly, Chol, Dopa, Sero, Nora, Hist) and to NT meaning carried by the CL head term (e.g. "GABAergic neuron").
  6. Combinations (Glut-Sero, Gly-Gaba, Gaba-Chol, Dopa-Gaba, Hist-Gaba, …): keep the one NT that applies to all clusters. If none does, drop the NT.
  7. NA (unannotated) clusters are ignored.
  8. The already-promoted CB PLI Gly-Gaba terms are included.
  9. This check changes names only; it doesn't remove terms from promotion.
  10. Redundancy. Remove taxonomy tokens that the CL head term already expresses:
  11. cell-class tokens such as Astro, Oligo, OPC, VLMC, MLI or PLI when the head says it;
  12. NN, always;
  13. CB/CBX when the head is "cerebellar …";
  14. an NT when the head implies it.
  15. Locations. Location acronyms stay as they are in names for now; expanded forms are far too long, especially with several regions. Checking and pruning them against regional summaries in Brain Cell KG is a later step.
  16. Numbers. Supertype _n suffixes stay where no distinguishing marker is available. Clusters already have markers folded in. Leading taxonomy numbers (0164 …) are dropped from final names; they survive in the synonyms.

docs.title: Step 0: Make the override explicit and tested
docs.text:
• defined_class_name shows up in the released wmbo-cl-comp.obo (e.g. CL:4300358 subcortical astrocyte (Mmus)). But no code in the repo reads it apart from the seeding of the curation table (src/scripts/template_generation_tools.py ~l.629). The DOSDP name is hard-coded to "%s %s (%s)".
  • Find where the override is applied today; it may be an uncommitted or removed step.
  • Then implement it explicitly: if defined_class_name is set, the label is exactly that value. Do the same for defined_class_definition. The released definitions appear to mix a curated first sentence with template clauses, so decide whether that is what we want.
  • Add a build check that every CL:43… label equals its override.

docs.title: Step 1: Build the evidence table
docs.text: Add a naming table to the cl_promotion/ machinery in the WMBv2 consensus repo, next to the promotion set. One row per promoted term: - the accession, level, v1 label, v2 label and merged singleton-chain members; - the CL parent ID and label, from the mapping step; - the current generated label; - the parent's final name; - the sibling v1 labels. - NT evidence: - NT tokens in the v1 label; - NT implied by the CL head; - the distribution of cluster neurotransmitter_accession values, ignoring NA; - the set of NTs present in every cluster. - Location and markers: location tokens, and cluster-level markers. - Existing override: any current defined_class_name. All 40 existing overrides are re-checked; SUBC_215 is already known to be wrong.

docs.title: Step 2: Deterministic pre-pass
docs.text: Apply the mechanical rules to produce a draft name: - drop the leading number and NN; - reduce NT combinations to the NT supported by every cluster, or none; - drop unsupported NTs; - remove tokens duplicated by the CL head; - attach the head noun. When the CL parent is generic ("neuron"), the head is the supported NT adjective + "neuron", e.g. PVH-SO-PVa Otp glutamatergic neuron; - add (Mmus).

docs.title: Step 3: Agent pass
docs.text: The agent works on the draft only where the rules leave something awkward: word order, duplicated or clashing tokens, siblings that become indistinguishable. - It may use only the evidence in the row; no new markers or regions. - It returns proposed_name, rationale, changes (tokens removed or added, and why) and confidence.

docs.title: Step 4: Automated checks (re-run on the final values)
docs.text:
• NT consistency of the final name, including any NT implied by the head term, against all non-NA clusters.
  • Redundancy: no token restates the head term.
  • Uniqueness within WMBO, and against existing CL labels via the OLS4 MCP.
  • Siblings under the same promoted parent have distinct names.
  • Format: (Mmus) suffix, no leading numbers, no NN.

docs.title: Step 5: Curator review → sheet
docs.text:
• Curators review the proposals, sorted by confidence and by failed checks.
  • Accepted names go into defined_class_name in the curation sheet. The sheet sync brings them into CCN20230722_class_curation.tsv.

docs.title: Step 6: Build and verify
docs.text: Rebuild. Check that: - every CL-promoted term's label equals its override; - the taxonomy label and the v2 label are exact synonyms; - the Step 4 checks pass on the released wmbo-cl-comp.obo.

docs.title: Later: checking locations against Brain Cell KG
docs.text: Location acronyms are inherited from the subclass label. Use the regional summaries in Brain Cell KG to find supertypes and clusters with few or no cells in a named region. Then prune those regions from names or definitions, and adjust the Locations axioms. This is a separate release.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• (Mmus) suffix: keep it on every CL-promoted name? The existing overrides mostly have it, but not all (e.g. CB PLI GABA_3 Gpr101 Purkinje layer interneuron).
  • NT form: spell NTs out ("glutamatergic") or keep taxonomy abbreviations ("Glut")? Spelled out reads better in CL; abbreviations match the synonyms.
  • Definitions: does this pass also write defined_class_definition, or leave the template definition?
  • Existing overrides: do all 40 get the same rules, including the CB PLI terms whose labels change?

docs.title: Curator Edit files:
docs.text:
• src/dendrograms/supplementary/version2/one_concept_one_name_curation.tsv: List the cell sets whose cells are identical. Enables curators to give them a single name.
  • src/dendrograms/supplementary/version2/CL_ontology_subset.tsv: Identifies the WMBO taxonomy terms that should be merged to the CL ontology. (This table generated by the src/dendrograms/supplementary/version2/cl_ontology_table_generator.py script.)

docs.title: WMBv2-informed CL promotion for WMBO (draft plan)
Context
docs.text:
WMBO is built from WMBv1 (CCN20230722, Yao 2023). By default its terms get PCL IDs (PCL_01…). A small curated subset is promoted to CL IDs (CL_43…); today that is 145 Add_to_CL=TRUE rows, which become 130 CL terms after singleton-chain collapse.

The promotion choices so far have been informal. The only record of them is free-text notes such as "Name holds true", "Major BG class" and "Adding all CB neurons to supertype level".

WMBv2 (CCN20251031) is a consensus of WMBv1 and the Broad/Macosko snRNA atlas. Its repo contains two things we can use: - a v1→v2 mapping based on shared-cell F1; - a per-node stability assessment that also checks each node against the Broad clustering, which is independent of v1.

Goal: use that evidence to choose, defensibly, which v1 types to promote to CL. For each promoted term: 1. make sure it is classified under a suitable, specific CL parent; 2. add its v2 name as a synonym.

The WMBO build otherwise stays as it is: same v1 source, same ID factories, same templates.

docs.title: Decisions already made
docs.text:
• Already-promoted terms (130 CL IDs): these are never demoted. Any that fail the stability criteria are listed in the report for curator review.
  • v2 name: added as oboInOwl:hasExactSynonym (changed from related on 2026-10-13: only terms judged sufficiently stable are promoted), with an axiom-annotation hasDbXref pointing to the CCN20251031 accession. This needs one new column in the DOSDP pattern.
  • Scope: a term must be both stable and CL-classifiable.
  • Subclass and supertype are the main targets.
  • Clusters are included only when triangulated, i.e. confirmed in Broad as well as v1 (tier S1 below).
  • Classes are excluded by default. A class is considered only if a curator marks it as easy to define and useful as a grouping class.
  • Conservative first pass: only 1:1 matches count; splits and merges are ignored. Stability is judged on independent Broad reproduction, not v1→v2 F1 alone (see Stability scoring).
  • First release: clusters need a stable parent (agreed 2026-09-29). A cluster stays in only if its v1 supertype or subclass is also in the promotion set.
  • This leaves 457 terms: 88 subclasses, 210 supertypes and 159 clusters (158 kept by the rule, plus 1 already in CL that has no promoted parent).
  • Classification then needs about 169 anchors (88 subclasses, 81 supertypes). The 23 clusters whose supertype isn't promoted are classified directly under their promoted subclass.
  • Neurotransmitter consistency is handled in naming, not selection. Terms aren't dropped for NT mismatches; unsupported NT mentions are removed from the final name instead. See docs/wmbo_cl_naming_plan.md.
  • Naming happens after promotion and CL mapping, before release. Every CL-promoted term gets a full defined_class_name override. See docs/wmbo_cl_naming_plan.md.
  • CL parents: gaps are filled by searching CL through the OLS4 MCP; a curator approves each choice (Step 1b).

docs.title: Inputs (all present locally)
docs.text:
<T> = WMBv2/target/whole_mouse_brain_consensus_taxonomy/

Input Path Use v1→v2 best match per level <T>/v1_to_v2_mapping/{class,subclass,supertype,cluster}_map_full.csv (v1_acc, best_v2, best_v2_name, f1, recall, precision_shared, …) per-v1-node F1, and the v2 name for the synonym v2 stability <T>/stability/{cluster,supertype,subclass}_stability.tsv (cluster: composite, tier; roll-ups: composite, frac_clusters_triangulated, frac_clusters_broad_confirmed) whether the v2 match is independently reproduced v2 CL mappings <T>/cl_mapping/cl_transfer_applied.csv, <T>/curation_tables/annotation.tsv (cell_ontology_term_id) suggested CL parents, including any new ones assigned in v2 v2 hierarchy WMBv2/WMB_v2_cas.json (parent_cell_set_accession) checking the hierarchy is preserved v1 taxonomy + CL mappings whole_mouse_brain_ontology/src/dendrograms/CCN20230722.json (sourced from the taxonomy repo's curation_tables/annotation.tsv) the current CL parent of each node or its nearest ancestor Current promotion list whole_mouse_brain_ontology/src/dendrograms/supplementary/version2/CL_ontology_subset.tsv (cell_set_accession, cell_label, Add_to_CL, Notes) baseline

Sheet sync: the promotion list, class_curation.tsv and the taxonomy's annotation.tsv are all pulled from Google Sheet 1LkeHNxWd5eltpbbYzH2aocMpnZjpIS7PpwXFk9d5ggg (google_sheets_to_tsv.py). Curation edits therefore have to go into the sheet, not the local TSVs. The assessment output is prepared for pasting or uploading into the sheet.

docs.title: Stability scoring: a conservative selection
docs.text:
Approach. For now we accept only 1:1 matches and don't model splits or merges. A v1 node qualifies on stability only if: - its best v2 match reproduces it (the gate), and - that v2 node is independently reproduced in the Broad/Macosko snRNA atlas.

v1→v2 F1 on its own is not enough. About 97% of v1 cells are carried into v2, and v2 kept the AIBS clustering strategy. The v1→v2 F1 is computed over those shared v1 cells only, so it mostly shows that integration didn't break the type. It is not independent evidence. Broad/Macosko snRNA nuclei are a large share of v2: macosko_frac has a median of about 0.46 per cluster. The Broad comparison is the independent evidence (different lab, assay and clustering pipeline), so it is what separates "stable" from "not contradicted".

docs.title: Gate (all levels)
docs.text:
• v1→v2 f1 ≥ 0.8 (from v1_to_v2_mapping/*_map_full.csv).
  • Reciprocal: the v2 node's own best-v1 F1 (v1_f1 in stability/*.tsv) equals the v1→v2 F1 to within 0.01. In the current data this holds for every F1 ≥ 0.8 match. It stays in as a guard against future mapping revisions.
  • The v1 parent's best v2 match is the v2 parent of best_v2 (hierarchy preserved).

docs.title: Evidence tiers
docs.text:
Each gated node gets a tier.

Clusters (Broad is tested natively at cluster level):

Tier Rule v1 clusters (of which already promoted) S1: promote tier = A_triangulated (Broad recall_loose ≥ 0.8 and strict F1 ≥ 0.8) and broad_tested_cells ≥ 50, so the Broad weight in composite is 1 210 (5) S2: review A_triangulated_loose, or A_triangulated with fewer than 50 Broad cells 263 (3) S3: not contradicted, untested C_v1_only_untestable (< 20 Broad cells) not promoted on stability alone exclude B_partial_broad, D_broad_discordant, E_weak_v1

An even stricter cut, composite ≥ 0.9 with ≥ 50 Broad cells, gives 136.

Supertypes and subclasses. Broad has no native levels here, so the evidence is rolled up from the node's v2 clusters.

The shipped roll-up columns can't be used as they are: - frac_clusters_broad_confirmed isn't normalised to n_broad_testable. Converted to "confirmed ÷ testable" it exceeds 1 for many nodes (e.g. Microglia, OPC, Astro-NT). The "confirmed" and "testable" definitions evidently use different cell thresholds. - The roll-up composite silently falls back to v1_f1 when nothing is testable (56 subclasses, 336 supertypes).

So we recompute the roll-up from cluster_stability.tsv, using the v2 parent links in WMB_v2_cas.json. For each v2 supertype or subclass: - broad_coverage = fraction of the node's cells in Broad-testable clusters (broad_tested_cells ≥ 20). Weighting by cells stops a few tiny untestable clusters from sinking a well-covered node. - broad_support = cell-weighted mean of broad_recall_loose over the testable clusters. - broad_discordant_frac = fraction of cells in clusters with broad_recall_loose < 0.5.

Tier Rule S1: promote gate passed, broad_coverage ≥ 0.5, broad_support ≥ 0.8, broad_discordant_frac ≤ 0.1 S2: review gate passed, broad_coverage ≥ 0.5, broad_support 0.6–0.8 S3: not contradicted, untested gate passed, broad_coverage < 0.5 exclude anything else

Rough size from the shipped roll-ups. Using F1 ≥ 0.8, coverage ≥ 0.5 and confirmed-rate ≥ 0.8, a first pass gives about 177 supertypes (21 already promoted) and 67 subclasses (12 already promoted). The recomputed cell-weighted numbers will differ. They are expected to be more generous to large non-neuronal subclasses, whose many small v2 clusters pull down cluster counts.

Known weakness. A containment test built up from clusters under-rates coarse types that Broad itself splits differently (glia, ependymal, choroid plexus). Several already-promoted non-neuronal subclasses fail the current roll-up even though the types are well established: Astro-NT, OPC, Microglia, VLMC, ABC, Hypendymal, CHOR and OEC. Two things follow. - Optional native test (later). Take the Broad cells in a v2 subclass or supertype and ask whether a union of Broad clusters covers the node with F1 ≥ 0.8. This needs the consensus cell-to-cluster membership from ABC, which isn't in the repo. The Broad metadata is local in WMBv2/Macosco_data/. - Curator review of S3 nodes. Treat S3 as "stable but untested". They are promotable only with extra evidence: an established CL type, literature, or spatial evidence, recorded in Notes.

Classes. No stability file exists at class level. A class needs the gate plus its subclasses mostly at S1 or S2 (≥ 50% of cells). It is only a curator-nominated grouping candidate.

docs.title: Lineage rule
docs.text:
• A supertype promoted at S1 whose parent subclass is not promoted is flagged. We may want the subclass as a grouping class, or a direct CL parent.
  • A cluster promoted without a promoted supertype or subclass above it is allowed. It must still pass the CL-classification check.

docs.title: Step 1: Assessment script (new, read-only analysis)
docs.text:
Status (2026-09-29): implemented, stability part only. The script lives in the WMBv2 consensus repo as whole_mouse_brain_consensus_taxonomy/cl_promotion/build_promotion_set.py, alongside stability/ and v1_to_v2_mapping/. It writes promotion_assessment.tsv, proposed_promotion_set.tsv, proposed_promotion_tree.md and summary.md; see that folder's README. CL classifiability (item 5) and Step 1b come later. Their results will update the v1 annotation table and WMBO's CL_ontology_subset.tsv.

Original design: It uses pandas plus OAK/pronto against cl.obo (already available through the ODK imports or mirror/).

The script builds one row for each v1 node (class, subclass, supertype, cluster) with the following fields.

  1. Mapping. best_v2, best_v2_name, f1, recall, precision, and the reverse v1_f1 for the reciprocity check. Splits and merges are not modelled.
  2. Hierarchy preserved. True if the v1 parent's best_v2 equals the v2 parent of best_v2, using the parent links in the CAS json.
  3. Stability evidence.
  4. Clusters: tier, composite, broad_tested_cells, broad_recall_loose, broad_f1_strict, macosko_frac.
  5. Supertypes and subclasses: the recomputed broad_coverage, broad_support and broad_discordant_frac, alongside the shipped roll-ups for comparison.
  6. stability_tier. S1, S2, S3 or exclude, as defined in the section above. Thresholds are CLI flags, and the report includes a sensitivity table.
  7. CL classifiability (automated part).
  8. cl_parent: the nearest cell_ontology_term_id on the node or an ancestor. This mirrors get_gross_cell_type() in src/scripts/template_generation_utils.py, so the script should import that function rather than reimplement it.
  9. cl_parent_source: self or ancestor:<acc>.
  10. Generic parents are flagged. Examples: CL:0000000, CL:0000540 neuron, CL:0000617 GABAergic neuron, CL:0000679 glutamatergic neuron, CL:0000125 glial cell. The flag also fires when the depth in CL is below a threshold.
  11. v2_cl_suggestion: the CL term assigned to best_v2 in v2's annotation.tsv or cl_transfer_applied.csv, if it differs from the v1 term or is more specific.
  12. Resulting cl_status:
    • ok: a specific parent exists.
    • needs_mapping: a suitable CL term exists but has to be added in the taxonomy sheet.
    • needs_NTR: no suitable CL term exists, so a new term request goes to the CL tracker.
  13. Current state. Whether the node is already Add_to_CL, and the existing notes.
  14. recommendation.
  15. promote: S1 and cl_status=ok.
  16. promote_after_mapping: S1, but the CL mapping or NTR has to happen first.
  17. review: S2, or S3 with supporting evidence.
  18. keep_existing_flag_review: already promoted but not S1.
  19. no.
  20. Collapsed singleton chains are resolved with the existing get_collapsed_nodes(), so each recommendation attaches to the node that will actually be minted. The chain's tier is its weakest member.

Outputs: - wmbv2_promotion_candidates.tsv: every row above. - cl_lookup_queue.tsv: the S1/S2 nodes whose cl_status is not ok. This is the input to Step 1b. - wmbv2_promotion_report.md: - counts by level, tier and recommendation; - existing CL terms that fail the criteria; - new candidates; - the list of CL mappings and NTRs needed; - the threshold sensitivity table.

docs.title: Step 1b: Finding CL parents with the OLS4 MCP (agent-assisted, curator-approved)
docs.text:
For each row in cl_lookup_queue.tsv, use the OLS4 MCP tools, restricted to ontology=cl, to find the most specific existing CL term the type can go under.

  1. Build queries from the taxonomy. Draw on:
  2. the neurotransmitter (Glut, GABA, Gly-Gaba, Chol, Dopa, Sero, …);
  3. region tokens (STR, CB, HY, MB, …), expanded to anatomy names;
  4. marker genes in the v1 and v2 labels (e.g. Sst, Pvalb, Car3);
  5. cell-class words (astrocyte, tanycyte, …).
  6. Search CL. Match on labels and exact synonyms. For each hit, retrieve its ancestors, and its definition and logical axioms where available (e.g. has soma location, capable of, has neurotransmitter), so candidates can be checked for consistency with the type.
  7. Rank and filter candidates.
  8. Prefer terms with mouse-applicable, transcriptomic or anatomical definitions.
  9. Reject species-restricted terms (e.g. human-only) and terms whose soma location or neurotransmitter disagrees with the type.
  10. Record the depth in CL, and whether the candidate is a descendant of the current cl_parent. It should be more specific than the current parent, not a sibling.
  11. Also look for already-existing CL:43… WMBO terms and CL:40… BICAN/CAP terms, to avoid duplicating a promotion.
  12. Output cl_candidates.tsv. One row per node, with up to 3 candidates:
  13. columns CL_id, label, match_basis, ancestors_ok, species_ok, confidence;
  14. match_basis is one of label | synonym | definition | axiom;
  15. confidence is high, medium or low.
  16. A curator makes the final choice.
  17. Where accepted choices go.
  18. A mapping on the node itself goes in the taxonomy annotation sheet: cell_ontology_term_id, rationale (cite the OLS match basis), rationale_dois. Use this only where the node is that CL type.
  19. Otherwise it goes in the WMBO Classification column (with Classification_comment), where the node is a subtype of the CL term. This avoids asserting equivalence in the published taxonomy.
  20. Nodes with no acceptable candidate become needs_NTR. A short NTR draft (label, parent, definition, markers, location, v1 and v2 accessions) goes in ntr_drafts.md.

Reproducibility. The OLS queries and the returned term IDs are logged with the CL release version that OLS reports, so the lookup can be re-run and diffed against later CL releases.

docs.title: Step 2: Curation (in the Google Sheet)
docs.text:
1. Add these columns to the WMBO_CL_ontology_subset tab: v2_accession, v2_label, f1, stability_tier, broad_support, cl_status, recommendation.
  2. get_cl_subset_nodes() in src/scripts/template_generation_tools.py reads only Add_to_CL, so extra columns are harmless.
  3. A curator sets Add_to_CL=TRUE for the accepted candidates. The Notes column records the basis, e.g. WMBv2 stable (F1=0.93, A_triangulated).
  4. CL parents:
  5. For needs_mapping, add cell_ontology_term_id, rationale and rationale_dois in the taxonomy annotation tab. The taxonomy CI then regenerates CCN20230722.json.
  6. Use the class-curation Classification column only as an override.
  7. needs_NTR terms go to the CL issue tracker. They wait for the new term before being promoted, or are promoted under the best available parent with a comment.
  8. For each newly promoted term, fill defined_class_name and, where possible, defined_class_definition in WMBO_CCN20230722_class_curation, as was done for the existing promoted terms. Classes considered as grouping classes need a definition before they are accepted.

docs.title: Step 3: Pipeline changes (minimal)
docs.text:
1. Mapping table for the build. Commit src/dendrograms/supplementary/version3/v1_v2_mapping.tsv with columns cell_set_accession, v2_accession, v2_label, f1, taken from the Step 1 output.
  2. Base template. In generate_base_class_template (src/scripts/template_generation_tools.py), load that table. For nodes in the CL subset only, emit two new columns:
  3. WMBv2_synonym (the v2 label);
  4. WMBv2_xref (CCN20251031:CS20251031_…, or whatever CURIE form the taxonomy RDF uses for accessions).
  5. DOSDP pattern. In src/patterns/dosdp-patterns/taxonomy_class.yaml:
  6. reuse the existing hasExactSynonym annotation property;
  7. add the two new vars to data_vars;
  8. add an annotation block that emits the exact synonym with a nested hasDbXref axiom annotation. This follows the existing nested-annotation pattern used for oboInOwl:evidence on the CL subClassOf.
  9. Checks on the rest of the build.
  10. wmbo-cl-comp filters with --select "annotations anonymous self", so the new annotations should carry through. This needs to be checked.
  11. IDs are unaffected: the CLIdFactory/PCLIdFactory ranges depend only on v1 node counts, and new promotions get an obsolete PCL twin automatically.
  12. The script should assert that newly minted CL_43… IDs don't collide with existing CL terms. Claude_analysis_reports/cl_module_generation_critical_report.md flags this as a risk.

docs.title: Step 4: Documentation
docs.text:
• This document is docs/wmbv2_cl_promotion.md. Once the plan is agreed, add it to the mkdocs.yaml nav.
  • Update the CL_ontology_subset section of docs/wmbo_workflow.md with the formal criteria.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
1. Run the Step 1 script and check the report against the input files.
  2. Row counts per level should be 34, 338, 1,201 and 5,322.
  3. The F1 bands should reproduce the README counts: subclass 268/41/29, and so on.
  4. Spot-check a few mappings, e.g. CS20230722_SUBC_318 Astro-NT and CS20230722_CLAS_28 CB GABA.
  5. Rebuild with cd src/dendrograms && make all (skip sheets if working offline), then run the release in src/ontology via sh run.sh make prepare_release.
  6. Checks on the new wmbo-cl-comp.obo against the current release:
  7. Count of CL:43 terms = 130 + the number of newly accepted terms.
  8. No existing CL ID is missing.
  9. Every CL term has an is_a to a CL term that is not in the generic list.
  10. Every newly promoted term has synonym: "<v2 label>" EXACT [CCN20251031:…].
  11. Every new promotion has an obsolete PCL twin in wmbo-base.
  12. Run robot reason / robot report on wmbo-cl-comp.owl to confirm there are no unsatisfiable classes and no new ERROR-level report items.

docs.title: Stability criteria
docs.text:
1. S1 thresholds.
  2. Clusters: A_triangulated with ≥ 50 Broad cells gives 210 clusters. Or the stricter composite ≥ 0.9, which gives 136?
  3. Supertypes and subclasses: cell-weighted broad_coverage ≥ 0.5 and broad_support ≥ 0.8. Confirm these once the recomputed roll-up is available. The report will include a sensitivity table.
  4. Is the roll-up test fair to coarse types? Rolling up containment from clusters under-rates types that Broad splits differently, such as glia, ependymal cells and choroid plexus. Should we run the native union-of-Broad-clusters test? It needs the consensus cell-to-cluster membership downloaded from ABC.
  5. S3 (not contradicted, untested in Broad). 362 clusters, plus supertypes and subclasses with low snRNA coverage. Should they be excluded outright for this release, or promotable with recorded external evidence?
  6. Broad-discordant nodes (D_broad_discordant, n = 79 clusters). These are excluded. Should an already-promoted term in this tier get anything stronger than a review flag?
  7. Splits and merges. Out of scope for this conservative pass. Revisit later, e.g. a v1 type that splits cleanly into several S1 v2 types could be a grouping class.
  8. Hierarchy preservation. It is currently part of the gate, so a term fails if its v1 parent maps to a different v2 parent. Keep it as a hard requirement or relax it to a flag?
  9. Classes. No class-level stability file exists. The draft rule is the gate plus ≥ 50% of cells in S1/S2 subclasses, then curator nomination. Which classes are the candidate grouping classes?
  10. Collapsed singleton chains. The draft takes the weakest member's tier. Agree?
  11. Already promoted terms that fail. From the shipped roll-ups, about 5 of 76 promoted clusters, 20 of 37 supertypes and 10 of 26 subclasses meet the strictest cut. Most of the failures are glial or cerebellar types that were promoted on prior-knowledge grounds. Keeping them as they are and adding a review flag is the current decision. Should the Notes column also record why each is retained?

docs.title: CL classification
docs.text:
1. Generic parents. Which CL terms count as "too generic"? The draft list is CL:0000000, neuron, GABAergic neuron, glutamatergic neuron and glial cell, plus a minimum depth in CL. Should a region-plus-neurotransmitter parent such as cerebellar neuron count as suitable?
  2. No suitable CL term. Should the promotion wait for a new CL term request (NTR) to be accepted, or go ahead under the best available parent with a comment? Who submits the NTRs, and should they be batched?
  3. Parents suggested by v2. Where the v2 CL mapping is more specific than or different from v1, adopt it automatically (added to the v1 annotation sheet with the same rationale) or only after curator review?
  4. Where CL mappings are written. The draft (Step 1b) splits them. When the node is the CL type, the mapping goes in the taxonomy annotation sheet, which changes the published CCN20230722. When the node is a subtype, it goes in the WMBO Classification column, which changes only the ontology. Is that split right?
  5. Names and definitions. Existing promoted terms have curated defined_class_name values, but only 4 have a curated definition. Should a curated definition be required for every new promotion, or is the auto-generated one ("A … of the … brain") acceptable?

docs.title: v2 synonym
docs.text:
1. Synonym format. v2 labels carry a numeric prefix and underscores, e.g. 0141 CLA-EPd-CTX_Car3_Glut 3. Keep the label verbatim, strip the number, or both?
  2. Which terms get the synonym. Only promoted terms, as in the draft, or every WMBO term that has a good v2 match (F1 ≥ 0.8)? The second is cheap and would help users navigate from v2, but it touches the PCL content.
  3. Cross-reference form. Which CURIE should point to the v2 node: CCN20251031:CS20251031_…, or the accession IRI used in the taxonomy RDF? Check the prefix is registered in the ontology's prefix map.
  4. Several v1 terms, one v2 node. When more than one v1 term matches the same v2 node, the same exact synonym lands on each of them. Is that acceptable, or should the synonym be added only for 1:1 matches?

docs.title: Process and build
docs.text:
1. Sheet workflow. Should the assessment columns go into the existing WMBO_CL_ontology_subset tab or a separate read-only tab? The first is convenient, but a sheet sync could overwrite script output.
  2. Where the mapping table is kept. The draft commits a static v1_v2_mapping.tsv copy into WMBO. The alternative is to fetch it from the WMBv2 repo at build time. A static copy is reproducible; fetching stays current if the v2 mapping is revised.
  3. ID collisions and stability. New CL_43… IDs depend on the CLIdFactory block layout. Check that no new ID collides with an existing CL term, and that none of the existing 130 IDs shift.
  4. Downstream. Should the new CL terms and synonyms be coordinated with the CL editors before release (for example, a CL PR importing wmbo-cl-comp), and with PCL/CAP so that both versions resolve consistently?
  5. WMBv2 in WMBO. Out of scope here, but should a later WMBO release be built from CCN20251031 directly? If so, promotions chosen now should stay compatible with that route.
